mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the cross-team possession asymmetry (Team B FOR ~56% all-prior, ~58.6% recent vs Team A FOR ~47% all-prior, ~47.8% recent) and simultaneously on Team B's recent shots surge (16.2 recent vs 13.5 all-prior) and shots-on-target surge (6.6 recent vs 4.8 all-prior). The mechanism asks whether, when one team holds a structural possession advantage AND shows a recent acceleration in shot volume, the ratio of shots-on-target to shots rises jointly — a two-observable joint relationship that cannot be reduced to either possession alone or shots alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team combines structural possession superiority with a recent surge in shot volume, its shots-on-target-to-shots ratio rises relative to its own all-prior baseline, more so than for the possession-inferior opponent
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession dominance (structurally higher than Team A's) combined with Team B's shot-volume surge in recent matches jointly predicts whether Team B's shots-on-target output rises disproportionately relative to its own historical conversion of possession into shots-on-target — i.e., the joint relationship between possession share and shots-on-target efficiency is tested across the two teams simultaneously rather than each in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession level AND shots volume trend) for both teams simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band — it tests whether the interaction of possession dominance and shot-volume acceleration predicts a non-additive lift in shot quality (shots-on-target rate).

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Team B produces 15.5 shots at home but only 11.0 away (all-prior), and 5.6 shots-on-target at home vs 3.8 away. Team A allows 13.4 shots against (all-prior). The mechanism conditions simultaneously on (a) Team B's home-vs-away shot drop (a within-team venue asymmetry across two observables) and (b) Team A's defensive shots-allowed level, asking whether the joint suppression effect — away venue penalty on Team B's shots AND Team A's defensive resistance — produces a non-additive reduction in Team B's shots-on-target beyond what either factor alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's shots-on-target away from home is suppressed relative to its home baseline, and this suppression is amplified when the opponent's shots-allowed average is at or below competition context — the two conditions jointly produce greater suppression than either alone
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The asymmetry between Team B's home-venue shot production and its away-venue shot production, when combined with Team A's defensive shot-allowance level, jointly determines whether Team B's away shots-on-target output is suppressed relative to its home baseline — testing a cross-observable, cross-venue asymmetric relationship between attacking volume and defensive resistance.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (shots and shots-on-target) conditioned on two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (venue asymmetry of the attacking team AND the defensive resistance of the opponent). It is not a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Team A concedes 0.267 goals in the first half but 0.833 in the second half (all-prior) — a 3x second-half elevation. Team B scores 0.667 in the first half and 0.767 in the second half (roughly balanced). The mechanism conditions on the joint within-match half-level split for both teams simultaneously: Team A's defensive vulnerability is concentrated in the second half, while Team B's attacking output is relatively front-loaded. The interaction of these two half-level profiles — not either alone — is the mechanism being tested.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's second-half defensive concession rate substantially exceeds its first-half rate AND the opponent (Team B) has a relatively balanced or first-half-weighted scoring profile, the second half of the match produces a disproportionate share of total goals relative to competition context norms
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half goal-concession rate is structurally elevated relative to its first-half rate, while Team B scores more goals in the first half than the second half proportionally — testing whether the within-match temporal goal-scoring asymmetry between the two teams (Team A leaks late, Team B scores early) jointly predicts a cross-half goal-distribution pattern that differs from the competition baseline.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (second half vs first half) applied jointly to two teams' asymmetric goal profiles — Team A's defensive half-split and Team B's offensive half-split — simultaneously. It is not a single observable with one coarse band; it is a joint two-team, two-half-period relationship.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Team A receives 1.5 cards in the second half (FOR) while conceding 2.067 cards against in the second half — both above the competition context of 1.811 per team. Team B commits 11.6 fouls away (all-prior) vs 9.7 at home, showing elevated away foul-rate. The mechanism conditions jointly on (a) Team A's second-half card-receiving tendency and (b) Team B's away foul-rate elevation, asking whether the combination of a high-fouling away team and a home team prone to second-half cards produces a joint uplift in second-half card volume beyond what either team's individual card or foul baseline would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half card volume rises above competition context when the away team's foul rate is elevated AND the home team's second-half card-receiving rate is above its own first-half baseline — the joint condition produces greater uplift than either factor alone
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team A's second-half card accumulation (cards_2h FOR elevated vs competition context) and Team B's foul-production level tests whether a high-fouling away team facing a home team prone to second-half cards produces a non-additive increase in second-half card volume — an asymmetric cross-observable mechanism linking one team's foul rate to the other team's card vulnerability.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-observable relationship: one team's foul production (Team B away) is linked to the other team's card-receiving vulnerability (Team A second-half), conditioned on a within-match period split. It involves two distinct observables across two teams and a half-level temporal dimension — not reducible to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on (a) Team B's recent corner surge (7.4 recent vs 5.0 all-prior, MODERATE reliability) and (b) Team B's structural home-vs-away corner asymmetry (5.6 home vs 4.3 away). The mechanism asks whether a team whose recent corner surge was accumulated predominantly in home matches (where corner production is structurally higher) reverts toward its away baseline when playing away — i.e., whether the recent trend and the venue dimension interact non-additively, with the venue correction partially or fully offsetting the recent surge. This is tested against Team A's corner-concession stability (3.9 all-prior, 4.0 recent).
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: A team's recent corner-kick surge is partially offset when playing away if its structural home-vs-away corner gap is large — the venue correction and the recent trend interact such that the away output does not sustain the full recent surge, showing saturation or regression relative to the recent window
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's corner-kick production shows a strong home-vs-away asymmetry (5.6 home vs 4.3 away all-prior) while also exhibiting a sharp recent surge (7.4 recent vs 5.0 all-prior). Team A's corner-kick concession rate is stable. The mechanism tests whether the joint condition of a team's recent corner-kick surge AND its structural home-advantage corner premium — when that team is playing away — produces a regression toward or below its all-prior away baseline, rather than sustaining the recent surge, revealing a non-linear saturation or venue-correction effect on corner-kick momentum.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct dimensions: the recent-vs-all-prior trend window AND the home-vs-away venue asymmetry, testing their interaction (non-additive suppression of the trend by venue). This is not a single observable with one coarse band — it is a threshold/saturation relationship between a continuous trend and a venue dimension.
